results.question: Which country takes the largest share of Sri Lanka's tea exports?
results.answer: Iraq took the largest share of Sri Lanka's tea exports in 2024, accounting for 10.9% of the total export value, which amounted to USD 149,621,564 out of USD 1,373,467,019 [1]. Sri Lanka exported tea to 145 destination markets in that year, indicating a diversified market presence with a Herfindahl concentration index of 0.05 [2]. The United Arab Emirates was the fastest-growing destination for Sri Lankan tea between 2020 and 2024, with an annual growth rate of 31.6% [3].

results.question: How fast have cinnamon exports grown over the last five years?
results.answer: Cinnamon exports from Sri Lanka contracted at a rate of 0.2% per year over the last four years, reaching a total export value of USD 214,425,881 in 2024 [5]. In that year, Mexico was the largest market, accounting for 38.4% of the export value, which equates to USD 82,418,643 [3]. Honduras was the fastest-growing destination for cinnamon exports between 2020 and 2024, with a growth rate of 7.7% per year [6]. There is no available data on cinnamon production at the district level, which limits the ability to provide more granular insights into production or export shares by district [2].

results.question: How concentrated are Sri Lanka's rubber export destinations?
results.answer: Sri Lanka's rubber export destinations are relatively diversified. In 2024, the country exported rubber worth USD 25,787,076 to 36 different markets [1]. Pakistan was the largest single market, accounting for 18.6% of the total export value, which amounted to USD 4,797,272 [1]. The Herfindahl concentration index for these exports is 0.11, suggesting a low level of concentration and indicating a diversified market [2]. Additionally, India was the fastest-growing destination for Sri Lankan rubber exports between 2020 and 2024, with an annual growth rate of 18.1% [3].
